meaning: From mustela (Latin) “weasel”, an ancient name for sharks, possibly referring to the pointed snouts, swift movements and/or rapacious feeding behavior of smaller predatory sharks
description: A fairly slender grey-brown shark with a white belly, a short head and snout and two large dorsal fins of similar size. It usually has no spots, unlike the starry smooth-hound it is often confused with. It lives on the seabed, mostly in the shallows, and feeds chiefly on crabs and other crustaceans.
eats: Mainly crabs and other crustaceans, also cephalopods such as squid and octopus, and bony fish
